title: The beta-zero strip DP is value-consistent on the exact DS18 law
statement: On the audited DS18 law X,Z iid Uniform[-1,1], S=(X,3X^2-1+Z), K=3, let z_tilde_N be the exact interval-DP labeling of the raw uncentered X_i=T_0,i. Almost surely it is regular eventually and Delta_N=v_hat_3,N(X)-Phi_hat_Ds(z_tilde_N)=I_hat_psilambda(z_tilde_N)^2/I_hat_lambdalambda(z_tilde_N)->0, because the empirical scalar-DP cells converge to the unique equal-third rule, the cross block tends to 0, and the nuisance block tends to 32/81. The audited DS18 finite-N disagreement inequality therefore applies to this polynomial-time labeling rule.
assumptions: the exact named DS18 law; d_psi=d_lambda=1; K=3; iid equal weights; exact scores
scores are not sample-centered and every empirical moment is about the origin
the DP uses beta=0 and exact scalar intervals; ties are null under the continuous X law

audited: the uncentered between value equals the centered between value plus the labeling-independent xbar^2, so z_tilde_N is exactly the empirical 3-means labeling of the X_i and DS18's selection-independent event Omega_0 applies to it without a profiled-optimality hypothesis

audited: the DS18 finite-N disagreement bound applies with the labeling's own Delta_N because z_tilde_N has own-codebook distortion excess 0 <= Delta_N; the bound was verified exactly on 12 dyadic samples up to N=4096

proof_location.section: DS19. The tilt-DP bracket: weak certification, an order-one gap, and a value-consistent DS18 primal

warning: Audited 2 Sep 2026: verified. Delta-consistency is a value statement only. It does not imply one-point exchange stability, selection by local ascent, perturbation robustness, or compile authorization.
